translation.OpeningReport.Title: Opening report
translation.OpeningReport.Intro: Study this position using the current local database and filters. Generate a theory table, inspect move orders and follow their reference games.
translation.OpeningReport.WaitForQuery: Select an exact position in a local database and wait for its query to finish.
translation.OpeningReport.Outcomes: White wins / draws / Black wins / unknown
translation.OpeningReport.Denominators: White score = (wins + half the draws) / known results. Frequencies include unknown results. Average Elo excludes missing ratings. These are game statistics, not an engine evaluation or a recommendation of the best move.
translation.OpeningReport.HistoryScope: Latest {{shown}} of {{total}} represented years within these matching games. This is not popularity relative to all games played that year. The HTML export includes every year.
translation.OpeningReport.Selection: Selected by highest mean Elo (both ratings required), then newest year, then lowest game ID. Games with incomplete ratings rank last. This is not a random or representative sample.
translation.OpeningReport.LinesShown: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} distinct lines, covering {{games}} games from the theory cohort.
translation.OpeningReport.ExcludedTheory: Selected games excluded from theory because they could not be decoded or the starting position exceeded 512 plies
translation.OpeningReport.CommonPrefix: An ellipsis repeats the previous row's move order up to the first divergence. Counts and scores in this table refer only to the selected theory cohort.
translation.OpeningReport.NoTheory: No readable theory lines are available for this selection.
translation.OpeningReport.CohortOnly: Move orders use the same selected theory cohort, not all matching games.
translation.OpeningReport.StartsHere: The game starts at this position
translation.OpeningReport.TranspositionScope: Different move orders converging on the same position at the same depth, within the selected theory horizon. Castling rights and legal en passant are preserved. Repetitions at different depths are not grouped here.
translation.OpeningReport.NoTranspositions: No transpositions were found within this cohort and depth. This does not mean none exist in the database.
translation.OpeningReport.Method: Main lines only; the first occurrence in each game is used. Different game IDs remain separate, including duplicate games. Statistics use all matching games; theory, move orders and transpositions use the ranked cohort. The file revision below identifies the local source state and is not a cryptographic dataset hash.
translation.OpeningReport.Saved: Export saved. The source database was not modified.
translation.OpeningReport.Expired: The query expired or the database changed. Refresh the position query and generate the report again.
translation.OpeningReport.Failed: The operation could not be completed. Try again, reduce the report depth or number of theory games, and check the export destination when saving.
translation.OpeningReport.EloBandsScope: The band uses both players' mean Elo. Only games with both ratings are included; {{unknown}} games could not be classified. Result percentages exclude unknown results.
translation.OpeningReport.PlayersScope: {{count}} distinct players across every matching game. Open one to inspect their games in a new tab. The database has no FIDE title field, so recorded Elo is used.
translation.OpeningReport.StrongestPlayersScope: Ranked by the highest Elo recorded in a matching game, even if they played the position only once.
translation.OpeningReport.HistoricalScope: This saved report is read-only. Its source data may have changed since the version was created.
translation.OpeningReport.EventFilterScope: Literal, case-insensitive event text. Percent signs and underscores are not treated as wildcards.
translation.OpeningReport.ModelGameMethod: Relevance is a transparent 0–100 heuristic: up to 70 points for mean Elo (capped at 3000), 20 for year (1900–2100), and 10 for continuation coverage. It ranks references; it is not an engine quality score.
translation.OpeningReport.DeviationScope: A deviation is the first move not seen from the same position in a strictly earlier dated game of the filtered report cohort. It is cohort-relative, limited by the selected theory-game cap, and is not a claim of historical novelty.
translation.OpeningReport.RemoteScope: This compact report uses only aggregates and references returned by Lichess. It does not download or scan the complete remote corpus, so it intentionally differs from a local report.
translation.OpeningReport.ReportOnlyFilters: Event and time-control filters apply only inside this report, so broader game and player drilldowns are disabled.

translation.GoMode.DepthTime.Desc: Easy positions stop at the depth, hard ones at the time cap. Depth 16 with 500 ms found the same errors as 500 ms per move, about 14% faster.
translation.Board.Database.BuildingIndex: Building the position index of this base (first search, or after its games changed): {{games}} games so far. It is done once.
translation.PlayerAnalysis.OpeningsRecalculate: Recalculate the profile to group the openings by family and variation.
translation.Board.Analysis.SecondPass: Second pass on the doubtful moves
translation.Board.Analysis.SecondPass.Desc: Analyzes again, deeper (depth 22, up to 1.5 s), the positions around the moves the first pass marked, at most 12 per game.
translation.Board.Analysis.CloudOpenings.Desc: Takes the evaluations of the first moves from the Lichess cloud, much deeper than the report, when it has them. Sends those positions to Lichess.

translation.Players.Habits.Title: Habits, clock and errors
translation.Players.Habits.Description: Descriptions of the games with their sample; they do not explain why something happens.
translation.Players.Habits.NextGame: Next game of the same day
translation.Players.Habits.NextGameSmall: Fewer than {{count}} games after a loss on the same day: not enough to compare.
translation.Players.Habits.NextGameSame: After a loss the next game scores about the same as usual.
translation.Players.Habits.NextGameLower: After a loss the next game scores {{gap}} points lower than usual ({{games}} games).
translation.Players.Habits.NextGameHigher: After a loss the next game scores {{gap}} points higher than usual ({{games}} games).
translation.Players.Habits.EndingsScope: The database does not store how a game ended. A loss with the loser to move, no mate and {{seconds}} s or less on their last clock reads as a probable time loss; only games with clocks can show it.
translation.Players.Habits.ClockHigh: More than a third of the base time
translation.Players.Habits.NoClocks: The analyzed games have no clock data ([%clk]) or no known base time.
translation.Players.Habits.ClockScope: Clock before each move as a share of the base time. Fast moves are measured from move {{from}} on, only with base+increment time controls.
translation.Players.Habits.NotLost: Losses in positions that were not lost
translation.Players.Habits.NotLostValue: {{count}} of {{losses}} analyzed losses without mate or probable time loss ended with the engine at −1.5 or better.
translation.Players.Habits.EngineMissing: Errors by move range, errors with little clock, fast moves and losses in positions that were not lost need an engine analysis of the games (Analysis tab).
translation.Players.Habits.Reanalyze: Analyses made before this version do not have it: analyze the sample again (the cache makes it quick).
translation.Players.Habits.RangeStandout: Errors concentrate in moves {{range}}: {{rate}} per 100 moves against {{overall}} overall.
translation.Players.Habits.RangeEven: No move range stands out from the rest.
translation.Players.HighlightsHint: Facts from the games in view. Click one to open its game.
translation.Players.Highlight.EngineMissing: They need an engine analysis of the games: run one in the Analysis tab.
translation.RatingPar.ColumnHint: Score minus the score the rating differences predict, in percentage points.
translation.Players.Openings.OpenBoard: Open the line on the board
translation.Players.Rivals.NoNemesis: No rival with {{count}}+ games and a negative balance
translation.Players.Rivals.NoFavourite: No rival with {{count}}+ games and a positive balance
translation.Players.Rivals.Scope: Nemesis and favourite opponent need {{count}} games. They are ranked by score against what the rating difference predicts, so a stronger rival is not a nemesis just for being stronger.
translation.Players.Rivals.AgainstYouHint: Games between this player and your own records in the same databases, from this player's side.
translation.Players.Rivals.AllHint: Click a row to see the games against that rival.
translation.Players.Rivals.MoreGames: And {{count}} more in the Games tab.
translation.Players.NotAnalyzedHint: None analyzed with the engine yet

translation.Players.NotEnoughRatings: Not enough rated months to draw the history.
translation.Generator.Difficulty.Tooltip: A {{elo}} opponent keeps the evaluation {{chance}}% of the time ({{basis}}). Moves that keep it: {{moves}}.
translation.Generator.Comment.Fallback: Few games here: the engine's move.
translation.Generator.Empty: Nothing to generate here: no move passed the engine check, or the source has no games.
translation.Generator.Focus.PracticalDesc: Score against what the rating difference predicts (local databases) or score, judged prudently by the sample.
translation.Generator.Focus.SolidDesc: Lowest share of losses, for events where losing costs the most.
translation.Generator.Focus.LowTheoryDesc: Moves that leave the opponent fewer replies to prepare for.
translation.Generator.Focus.EngineDesc: The engine's best among the moves with enough games.
translation.Generator.Focus.TrickyDesc: Positions where an opponent of the chosen rating is least likely to find a good move.
translation.Generator.Focus.SurpriseDesc: Rare moves the engine still likes, the hardest for the opponent first.
translation.Generator.Source.Login: The Lichess explorer needs a Lichess account connected with browser login (Accounts).
translation.Generator.Focus.WithoutMaia: Without Maia, only positions with enough games are judged.
translation.Generator.Surprises.MySide: Only my moves (the side I play)
translation.Generator.SurpriseShare: A surprise is at most (% of games)
translation.Generator.Provenance: Generated by Onyx on {{date}} from {{source}}. Focus: {{focus}}. Opponent: {{opponent}}. Engine: {{engine}}, {{ms}} ms per position, at most {{loss}} cp from its best move. Depth {{depth}} half-moves, {{games}} games to trust a move.
translation.Generator.SavedHint: Find it in Training → Openings, ready to review and learn.
translation.Generator.Surprises.Title: Surprises
translation.Generator.Phase.Maia: Asking Maia how an opponent would reply…
translation.Generator.Title: Repertoire generator
translation.Generator.Mode.RepertoireHint: From the board position: one move of yours in each position, chosen by the focus and checked by the engine, and the opponent's likely replies.
translation.Generator.Mode.SurprisesHint: Along the board line: moves the engine keeps close to its best that the source rarely or never plays, the hardest for the opponent first. Idea from Matthew Sadler's Novelty Grinder.
translation.Generator.NoEngine: Install a reference engine such as Stockfish in Engines.
translation.Generator.NoMaia: Maia 3 is not installed: replies and difficulty come only from the games of the source.
translation.Generator.Idle: Choose the settings and run it. Nothing is saved until you create the repertoire or open the result.
translation.Generator.Name: Repertoire name
translation.Generator.Surprises.Stopped: Stopped at move {{move}}: fewer than {{games}} games in the source.
translation.Generator.Surprises.None: No surprise passed the filters in this line. Try a higher share, a larger engine margin or an earlier move.
translation.Generator.Surprises.Provenance: Surprises found by Onyx in {{source}}: at most {{share}}% of the games, within {{loss}} cp of the engine's best. Red arrow: no games; green: rare.
translation.Generator.Difficulty.Comment: For a {{elo}} opponent: {{chance}} keep the evaluation ({{level}}; {{basis}}).
translation.Generator.Comment.Novelty: Surprise: no games in the source.
translation.Generator.Focus.Slower: Slower: it checks every candidate with the engine and asks Maia where the source has few games (a few seconds per position).
translation.Preparation.Book.Title: Likely repertoire
translation.Preparation.Book.Description: The moves of {{name}}'s games with each color, with the score and rating par of {{name}} after each one. Badges mark recent deviations.
translation.Preparation.Book.Empty: No games with this color in the current filters.
translation.Preparation.Book.NoMoves: No game of the filters continues from here (the book reads the first ten moves).
translation.Preparation.Book.NewHint: First played on {{date}}, in the last three months of these games.
translation.Preparation.Book.ParHint: Score of {{name}} minus the one the ratings predict, in {{count}} rated games.
translation.Preparation.Book.Legend: Bar: share of the games. Then wins, draws and losses of {{name}}, score and rating par.
translation.Preparation.HowTo.Targets: These are the places where {{name}} has scored below what the ratings predicted. Steering the game there is a reasonable plan, not a guarantee.
translation.Preparation.HowTo.PlayYourRepertoire: Nothing clearly below par in these games: no line, structure or phase stands out. Play your repertoire.
translation.Preparation.HowTo.TooFew: Too few games for a verdict ({{count}}). Add more games of this player or widen the filters.
translation.Preparation.HowTo.Title: How to play against {{name}}
translation.Preparation.HowTo.Description: Lines, structures and kinds of game where the score is at least 5 points below the one the ratings predict, with at least 10 rated games.
translation.Preparation.HowTo.NoOpenings: No opening with enough rated games stands out.
translation.Preparation.HowTo.NoStructures: Nothing below par with enough rated games.
translation.Preparation.HowTo.NeedsEngine: Needs an engine analysis of these games (Analysis tab).
translation.Preparation.HowTo.WorstPhase: Most errors in the {{phase}}: {{rate}} mistakes or blunders per 100 moves against {{average}} on average ({{moves}} moves).
translation.Preparation.HowTo.NoWorstPhase: No phase has clearly more errors than the others.
translation.Preparation.HowTo.BestPhase: Fewest errors in the {{phase}}: {{rate}} per 100 moves.
translation.Preparation.Key.TitleSelf: Where I tend to go wrong
translation.Preparation.Key.Title: Key positions for {{name}}
translation.Preparation.Key.DescriptionSelf: The positions your most played lines reach with you to move, and the chance that a player of your level keeps the evaluation there. The lowest ones are the first to train.
translation.Preparation.Key.Description: The positions {{name}}'s most played lines reach with {{name}} to move, and the chance that a player of that level keeps the evaluation. The lowest ones are where it pays to take the game.
translation.Preparation.Key.NoMaia: Maia 3 is not installed: positions with fewer than {{count}} games of this player are left without a difficulty.
translation.Preparation.Key.Empty: No position is reached often enough (at least 3 games and 4% of the games with this color).
translation.Preparation.Key.Idle: Press the button to measure them: Stockfish marks the moves that keep the evaluation and the player's own choices (from {{count}} games in the position) or Maia at the chosen level say how often they are found.
translation.Preparation.Package.PlayYour: Nothing clearly below par: play your repertoire.
translation.Preparation.Package.Caution: A summary of trends in past games, not a certainty: check every line.
translation.Preparation.Package.Legend: Moves of {{name}}'s games. Each comment: games / games in the position · score of {{name}} · rating par · last game.
translation.Preparation.Reality.Title: My repertoire against {{name}}
translation.Preparation.Reality.DescriptionSelf: Where your games leave your Onyx repertoires: a different move of yours is a forgotten line; a reply the repertoire does not cover is a gap in the preparation.
translation.Preparation.Reality.Description: The replies {{name}} actually plays that your Onyx repertoire does not answer, most played first.
translation.Preparation.Reality.NoRepertoire: No Onyx repertoire with this color starts from the initial position. Create one in Training → Openings (or with the generator) to compare it.
translation.Preparation.Reality.NoExits: Every game stays inside the repertoire until it ends or the book ends.
translation.Preparation.Reality.OpenHint: Open the line on the board, where “Add to repertoire” adds it.
translation.Preparation.Structures.Title: Pawn structures
translation.Preparation.Structures.Description: Eight named structures, looked for between moves 12 and 25 and counted when they hold for three moves. {{name}} has them (with) or faces them (against).
translation.Preparation.Structures.Experimental: The rules are approximate and still being validated against labelled example games. Hover a structure to see its rule.
translation.Preparation.Structures.Empty: None of the eight structures appears in these games (games shorter than 15 moves cannot have one).
translation.Preparation.Structures.Coverage: {{count}} of {{total}} games have at least one of these structures.
translation.Preparation.Structures.EndgameRule: No queens and at most six pieces besides kings and pawns, as Player Analysis defines the endgame.
translation.Preparation.Twin.Name: Twin of {{name}}
translation.Preparation.Twin.Title: Play against the twin
translation.Preparation.Twin.Description: A bot that plays {{name}}'s repertoire (the opening sequences of these games, with their real frequency) and, out of it, like a player of that rating. It does not imitate {{name}}'s individual style beyond the book.
translation.Preparation.Twin.NoMaia: The twin needs Maia 3. Install it from Engines (managed installation).
translation.Preparation.Twin.Honest: Ratings from other sites or over the board do not match Maia's scale exactly: adjust the level if it feels off.
translation.Preparation.Twin.FidelityHint: The most recent 20% of the games are left out of the book. In each of {{name}}'s positions inside the book, how often the twin would play the move really played, against plain Maia at the same rating. Out of the book the twin is Maia, so both match there.
translation.Preparation.Twin.FewGames: At least 15 games with this color are needed.
translation.Preparation.Twin.NoBookPositions: None of the test games stays in the book: the twin plays like Maia from the first move.
translation.Preparation.Twin.Better: Inside the book the twin reproduces {{name}}'s moves clearly better than plain Maia.
translation.Preparation.Twin.Same: The twin does not improve on plain Maia here: {{name}}'s repertoire is close to what that rating usually plays, or too varied.
translation.Preparation.Twin.Worse: The book reproduces these games worse than Maia: the recent games depart from the older ones.
translation.Preparation.Twin.Sample: {{positions}} positions in the book ({{sampled}} measured, {{samples}} Maia samples each), {{out}} moves out of the book; book from {{train}} games, test with {{test}}.
translation.Preparation.Note.Title: Guidance, not a certainty
translation.Preparation.Note.BodyGames: A summary of trends in {{count}} past games. Rivals change, prepare surprises and play differently over the board: use it as a starting point and check every line yourself.
translation.Preparation.Note.Body: A summary of trends in past games. Rivals change, prepare surprises and play differently over the board: use it as a starting point and check every line yourself.
translation.Preparation.StructureRule.Iqp: A lone d-pawn on the fourth rank with no own c- or e-pawns; the opponent has no d-pawn.
translation.Preparation.StructureRule.Carlsbad: d4 and e3 (or e2) without a c-pawn against c6 (or c7) and d5 without an e-pawn: the minority-attack side owns it.
translation.Preparation.StructureRule.Hanging: c- and d-pawns side by side on the fourth rank, no own b- or e-pawns, no enemy c- or d-pawns.
translation.Preparation.StructureRule.CaroSlav: c6 and e6 without a d-pawn against d4, with White missing the e-pawn (Caro-Kann) or the c-pawn (Slav).
translation.Preparation.StructureRule.Maroczy: c4 and e4 without a d-pawn against a d-pawn and no c-pawn (a Sicilian set-up).
translation.Preparation.StructureRule.Hedgehog: a6, b6, d6 and e6 against c4 and e4.
translation.Preparation.StructureRule.KingsIndian: The closed chain d6/e5 against d5/e4.
translation.Players.RivalGames.Title: Add games of {{name}}
translation.Players.RivalGames.Description: The games go into a local database; then choose which player in it is {{name}}. The preparation does not need a reference database.
translation.Players.RivalGames.BroadcastHint: Official Lichess broadcasts of over-the-board tournaments (CC BY-SA). All rounds of the chosen tournaments go into the “Lichess broadcasts” database.
translation.Players.RivalGames.Ready: Games saved in “{{title}}”. Choose the player's records:
translation.Players.RivalGames.NoRecords: No player with those words in this database.
translation.RepertoireDifficulty.Title: Hard positions for me · {{name}}
translation.RepertoireDifficulty.Description: The positions of this repertoire where it is your move, and the chance that a player of your level finds a move that keeps the evaluation. The lowest ones are the first to practice. An estimate from Maia and the engine, not a measure of your own memory.
translation.RepertoireDifficulty.NeedsEngines: It needs a reference engine such as Stockfish and Maia 3, both from Engines.
translation.RepertoireDifficulty.Empty: This repertoire has no theory moves of this color.
translation.RepertoireDifficulty.DubiousHint: The engine does not count the prepared move among those that keep the evaluation ({{loss}} cp from its best). Worth reviewing.
translation.RepertoireDifficulty.ButtonHint: Positions of this repertoire where a player of your level is most likely to go wrong (Stockfish and Maia).
translation.Generator.Rival.Title: Against {{name}}
translation.Generator.Rival.Hint: Their replies come from their games (Maia at {{elo}} where they have too few). Your moves are chosen by how {{name}} did against each one, always checked with the engine.
translation.Preparation.Twin.Summary: Plays {{name}}'s repertoire ({{lines}} sequences from {{games}} games) and, out of it, like a player of that rating (Maia).
translation.Preparation.Twin.NotLoaded: The twin's book is no longer in memory: open it again from the player card, or it will play as plain Maia.
translation.Diagnosis.LeakEvidence: {{errors}} errors, {{cost}} points of winning chances in {{games}} analyzed games.
translation.Diagnosis.PhaseEvidence: {{rate}} mistakes or blunders per 100 moves against {{average}} on average ({{moves}} moves).
translation.Diagnosis.LowClockEvidence: {{low}} errors per 100 moves with less than 10% of the time, against {{rest}} with more ({{moves}} moves with little time).
translation.Diagnosis.ConversionEvidence: {{rate}}% of {{games}} games with +1.5 or more were won (priority below 70%).
translation.Diagnosis.DefenseEvidence: {{rate}}% of {{games}} games at −1.5 or worse were drawn or won (priority below 30%).
translation.Diagnosis.Title: Training priorities
translation.Diagnosis.Description: What to train first, each item with its evidence and a concrete step. The order is fixed: first the costliest leak and the weak phases the engine measured, then conversion and defense, then results without the engine (openings and time controls).
translation.Diagnosis.NoEngine: Without an engine analysis of these games only the results are diagnosed (openings and time controls).
translation.Diagnosis.Nothing: Nothing stands out with enough sample in these games. Keep reviewing the queue and analyze more games.
translation.Diagnosis.Sample: {{games}} games in the filters, {{analyzed}} analyzed with the engine. Templates over measured facts: no AI writes or decides these items.
translation.Leaks.Title: Leaks
translation.Leaks.Description: The mistakes and blunders of the analyzed games, each in the most specific category whose rule holds, the costliest first. What no rule can check stays unclassified.
translation.Leaks.NeedsEngine: Leaks need an engine analysis of the games in these filters.
translation.Leaks.MissingData: {{count}} errors come from analyses made before this version, without the winning chances before the move or the clock: some categories cannot be checked for them. Analyze the sample again (the cache makes it quick).
translation.Leaks.CostHint: Points of winning chances given away in total, and per analyzed game.
translation.Leaks.TurnedHint: Lost games with an error of this category made from 40% winning chances or more.
translation.Leaks.Sample: {{games}} analyzed games, {{moves}} moves of the player. No comparison with other players: Onyx has no reference games with the same time control, level and engine settings, and without them the comparison would mislead.
translation.Leaks.TrendHint: Errors of the four costliest categories per 100 moves; quarters with fewer than 100 analyzed moves are left out.
translation.Leaks.TrendEmpty: It needs analyzed games in at least two quarters. Analyze games from different periods to see it.
translation.Mistakes.NothingNew: No new errors in this analysis.
translation.Mistakes.Title: My mistakes
translation.Mistakes.Description: The errors of the analyzed games as exercises: find a better move than the one played. Each comes back by spaced repetition until it is learned; the same position counts once, whatever the number of games.
translation.Mistakes.ClearConfirm: Empty the queue? Its progress is lost and these positions are not added again automatically.
translation.Mistakes.AutoAdd: Add errors automatically after each engine analysis
translation.Mistakes.AutoAddHint: Mistakes and blunders of this card; removed items do not come back.
translation.Mistakes.EmptyWithAnalysis: The queue is empty. Add the errors of the current analysis or turn on the automatic addition.
translation.Mistakes.EmptyNoAnalysis: The queue fills from the engine analysis of the games: analyze some games first.
translation.Mistakes.Session.Title: Review my mistakes
translation.Mistakes.Session.DoneSummary: {{solved}} of {{total}} found. They come back when they are due.
translation.Mistakes.Session.Prompt: In the game you played {{move}}. Find a better move.
translation.Mistakes.Session.Same: That is the move of the game. Try another one.
translation.Practice.Title: Conversion and defense
translation.Practice.Description: Your own positions to play again against Maia at the level of that game's opponent: where you were clearly better (+1.5) and did not win, to convert; where you were clearly worse (−1.5), to defend.
translation.Practice.NeedsEngine: The positions come from the engine analysis of the games.
translation.Practice.Reanalyze: {{count}} analyzed games are from before this version and do not keep the position: analyze them again to include them.
translation.Practice.ConvertGoal: Goal: win the position. These are the advantages of the analyzed games that ended in a draw or a loss.
translation.Practice.DefendGoal: Goal: draw or better. The lost games come first.
translation.Practice.NoDefense: No analyzed game reached a clearly worse position.
translation.Practice.Honest: Maia plays like a human of that rating, not the real opponent; its scale is that of Lichess.
translation.Leaks.Rule.allowedMate: The engine's reply line ends in mate against you. A mistake or worse (10+ points of winning chances).
translation.Leaks.Rule.missedMate: The engine's best line was a forced mate for you.
translation.Leaks.Rule.hangingPiece: The opponent's best reply takes a piece of yours (a knight or more) that nothing can take back.
translation.Leaks.Rule.allowedFork: The opponent's best reply puts a piece on a square that attacks two of your pieces worth a knight or more (or the king).
translation.Leaks.Rule.missedFork: The engine's best move was a fork of two enemy pieces worth a knight or more (or the king).
translation.Leaks.Rule.missedCapture: The engine's best move captured an enemy piece worth a knight or more.
translation.Leaks.Rule.missedPromotion: The engine's best move was a promotion.
translation.Leaks.Rule.conversion: From 80% winning chances or more, the move left you below 60%.
translation.Leaks.Rule.collapse: In a worse but defendable position (10–40% winning chances), a mistake or worse.
translation.Leaks.Rule.timeTrouble: Less than 10% of the base time on your clock.
translation.Leaks.Rule.opening: In the first ten moves, with no more specific category.
translation.Leaks.Rule.endgame: In the endgame, with no more specific category.
translation.Leaks.Rule.unclassified: No rule above can be checked for this error: it keeps its loss, without a cause.
translation.Players.EngineBadge.Open: Open the engine analysis: see its games or analyze more of them.
translation.Mistakes.AlreadyThere: That position is already in the queue.
translation.Endgame.Mate.FailedDesc: The clock ran out, or the defense reached a draw. A new position is one click away.
translation.Endgame.Verdict.Unavailable: The verdict is not available: no tablebase connection and no local engine.
translation.Endgame.Watch.LostDescExact: Against the best defense the objective can no longer be reached.
translation.Endgame.Watch.LostDescEngine: The engine no longer sees the objective as reachable against the best defense.
translation.Continuous.Title: Continuous review
translation.Continuous.Note: The opponent steers towards your weakest moves. Spaced reviews are not affected.
translation.Puzzle.Candidates.Question: Which move?
translation.Puzzle.OutdatedDesc: This database does not support themes. Update to the latest puzzle database.
translation.Puzzle.RushRange: In storm and streak the difficulty rises on its own.
translation.Puzzle.Candidates.Desc: Choose the first move among a few plausible ones, as a player of that level would see them.
translation.Puzzle.Mode.FreeDesc: At your own pace. The first try of each puzzle counts for your tactical rating.
translation.Puzzle.Mode.CountdownDesc: The same time for every puzzle; running out counts as a miss.
translation.Puzzle.Mode.StormDesc: Solve as many as you can before the clock ends. Each one is harder; a mistake costs 10 s.
translation.Puzzle.Mode.StreakDesc: Each puzzle is harder than the last. A mistake costs a life.
translation.Puzzle.DeleteDatabaseDesc: Are you sure you want to delete this puzzle database?
translation.Puzzle.NoMatch: No puzzle matches these filters. Widen the rating range, the themes or the quality.
translation.Puzzle.TacticalRatingTip: Glicko-2 against the rating of each puzzle, first try only, in free and countdown modes.
translation.Endgames.Mates.Description: A new random position each time. The lone king defends as well as possible and the 50-move rule counts: mate before your clock runs out.
translation.Endgames.Import.Title: Import endgames
translation.Endgames.Import.ComputeDesc: Tablebase up to 7 pieces, Stockfish above. An objective written in the PGN is kept; if the calculation disagrees, you will see a notice.
translation.Endgames.Sets.Description: Your imported endgames. Their positions also appear by theme.
translation.Endgames.Sets.EmptyHint: A PGN can hold a whole book: you can split it by theme or chapter when importing.
translation.Endgames.Page.Subtitle: Reach the objective against the best defense: each move is checked as you play.
translation.Continuous.MenuDesc: No end and no grades: the opponent steers towards your weakest moves. Spaced reviews are not affected.
translation.Gaps.ButtonTip: Opponent replies your repertoire does not answer, by how often they come up.
translation.Gaps.Title: Coverage of {{name}}
translation.Gaps.Description: Opponent replies your repertoire does not answer, ordered by how often you will meet them. Where a line ends on purpose, nothing is reported.
translation.Gaps.None: No uncovered replies above {{share}} % of the games. Your repertoire answers what usually comes up.
translation.Gaps.Column.WeightTip: Chance of reaching the position times the share of the reply.
translation.Gaps.Footer: “Add by hand” opens the position on the board: play your reply and use “Add to repertoire”. “Generate” builds a few lines from there with the repertoire generator, which you can review and add the same way.
translation.Tactics.Builder.None: No puzzle matches these filters. Widen the band, the themes or the quality.
translation.Tactics.Builder.Title: New set from the puzzle database
translation.Tactics.Builder.NoDatabase: Install the Lichess puzzle database first (puzzle trainer → add database).
translation.Tactics.Builder.MaxPiecesDesc: Optional; fewer pieces make visualization easier
translation.Tactics.Progress.NoRating: Solve puzzles in the trainer (free or countdown) to get one.
translation.Tactics.Progress.Next: Next one in {{interval}} · {{total}} in the review
translation.Tactics.Progress.Empty: Missed puzzles and exercises will come back here.
translation.Tactics.Progress.AutoAddTip: Missed puzzles of the trainer and exercises of your sets join the review on their own.
translation.Tactics.Review.Title: Tactics review
translation.Tactics.Review.Summary: {{solved}} solved at the first try, {{hard}} with help and {{failed}} missed. Missed ones come back soon.
translation.Tactics.Review.Missed: Not that one. It will come back soon; try again to finish it.
translation.Tactics.Review.Solved: Solved. It will come back later.
translation.Tactics.Visual.BlindUnavailable: Blind needs to know what led to the position: puzzles that start with the opponent's move or exercises from your games.
translation.Puzzle.ExcludeThemesDesc: Puzzles with any of these themes never appear.
